scope: whole project (App Router, Next.js latest, React latest, TypeScript strict)

findings.title: Card counts read from the query result object instead of the first row
findings.explanation: sql`SELECT COUNT(*) ...` is untyped, so data[0] is the postgres.js result array (RowList), not a row. Its `.count` property is the number of returned rows (1 for an aggregate query), not the COUNT(*) value, which lives in data[0][0].count. The untyped result lets this compile, so the dashboard cards 'Total Invoices' and 'Total Customers' would show 1 instead of the real totals. The same file reads data[0].count in fetchInvoicesPages, where data is a RowList, so that call has the right shape. Assumption: postgres.js RowList.count semantics (rows returned for SELECT).
findings.evidence:
const numberOfInvoices = Number(data[0].count ?? '0');
    const numberOfCustomers = Number(data[1].count ?? '0');
findings.suggested_fix: Type the queries (for example sql<{ count: string }[]>) and read the first row: Number(data[0][0].count ?? '0') and Number(data[1][0].count ?? '0').

findings.title: Search label points to an id that the input does not have
findings.explanation: The label uses htmlFor="search" but the <input> has no id, so the label is not associated with the field. The field only has a placeholder as a fallback name, which is not a reliable label, and clicking the label does not focus the input. The component is used on the invoices and customers pages.
findings.suggested_fix: Add id="search" to the <input> (or wrap it in the label).

findings.title: Icon-only links have no accessible name (edit invoice, pagination arrows)
findings.explanation: UpdateInvoice renders a Link whose only content is a decorative heroicon, with no text, aria-label or visually hidden text, so screen-reader users hear an unnamed link for every table row. The same pattern appears in app/ui/invoices/pagination.tsx lines 120-122, where the previous/next arrow Link contains only an icon. DeleteInvoice in the same file shows the intended pattern with an sr-only span.
findings.evidence:
<Link
      href={`/dashboard/invoices/${id}/edit`}
      className="rounded-md border p-2 hover:bg-gray-100"
    >
      <PencilIcon className="w-5" />
    </Link>
findings.suggested_fix: Add a visually hidden label such as Edit invoice (or aria-label) inside the link. Do the same for the previous/next page arrows in pagination.tsx.

findings.title: Nav links and Sign Out button lose their text name below the md breakpoint
findings.explanation:
The link text is in an element with Tailwind `hidden md:block`, which is display:none on small screens. Display:none content is excluded from the accessibility tree, so on mobile each nav link contains only a decorative icon and has no accessible name. The Sign Out button in app/ui/dashboard/sidenav.tsx lines 28-29 uses the same pattern (
Sign Out
). Assumption: Heroicons render with aria-hidden and the project has no other label.
findings.suggested_fix: Use sr-only plus md:not-sr-only (or an aria-label on the Link and button) so the name stays available when the text is visually hidden.

limitations: Source review only: nothing was built or run, so F1 (postgres.js RowList.count behaviour) and F4 (icon aria-hidden defaults) rely on library behaviour not verified here.
No ESLint config is present in the project root, so jsx-a11y and react-hooks lint coverage could not be assessed.
Color contrast, focus appearance and screen-reader output were not evaluated.
app/ui/skeletons.tsx, app/ui/acme-logo.tsx, app/lib/placeholder-data.ts, app/lib/definitions.ts and styling files were only skimmed or searched, not read line by line.
Security, authorization and business-logic topics (SQL access, delete without error handling, unauthenticated seed/query routes, currency math) are out of scope for this skill and were not reported.
package.json uses next/react 'latest', so the exact framework version, and behaviour tied to it, could not be determined.
